name: Rio Tinto Group
executive_summary:
Rio Tinto Group is a dual-listed bulk-commodity major (LSE:RIO / ASX:RIO / NYSE:RIO) in iron ore, copper, aluminium and lithium. The quantitative screen still prints strong_buy: 11/22 models, composite 0.679 versus a sector-relative 0.725, five families (cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, risk). That label is not clean. The same 2 September 2026 run’s screen_run_manifest adjusts the signal to buy at conviction 0.439 after FCF Yield (score 0.30) and Earnings Quality fail, while the snapshot overwrites that brake to strong_buy and conviction 0.689, leaves failed_models empty, and seeds duplicated “Accumulate, Medium risk” boilerplate. Every cyclical and dividend-yield overlay flag is false on an iron-ore/copper/aluminium/lithium name. Timing is neutral (RSI 53.5, price +0.08% versus the 200-day average, price above the 50- and 200-day averages). The signal is one week old, stability new, trend improving, since 2 September 2026. This trial re-asks an unchanged 4 September 17:26Z catalog; no Q3 production RNS has arrived.

The assigned “annual” body is not the statutory 2025 Annual Report. It is an Investegate notice that the report was released on 19 February 2026. No segment, cash-flow or balance-sheet tables are on that page. The usable filing is the 29 July 2026 H1 results: underlying EBITDA $14.8 billion (+28%), underlying earnings $6.9 billion (+43%), free cash flow $3.8 billion (+75%) on a refined company definition, net debt $14.1 billion, and a 50% payout interim of $3.4 billion. Copper, aluminium and lithium together were more than half of group underlying EBITDA. 2026 shipment, Pilbara unit-cost and capex guidance was maintained, not cut; the copper C1 unit-cost range was reduced on 15 July and the effective-tax guide was lowered to about 25%.

Do not endorse the fresh strong_buy. Screen FCF of 3,596 million disagrees with Yahoo FY2025 FCF of 4,497 million, and both sit below Yahoo cash dividends paid of 6,145 million. H1 company FCF of $3.8 billion covers the $3.4 billion interim declared but not the $4.2 billion of 2025 final dividend cash paid in the half. News on 2 September already frames the stock as DCF-rich / fully valued on the critical-minerals narrative after a ~£75.77 print, +6.9% over 30 days, +26.6% year-to-date and +72% one-year total return. Summary trade limits of £7,153.82 / £6,905.37 (stop £6,678.72, target £7,858.20) match pence (ATR 198.6), not pounds. Accumulate on the H1 mix-shift and held guidance; treat the screen’s strong_buy and the pence-as-pounds ladder as unsafe until the unread FY pack, Q3 production and FCF-versus-dividend path are reconciled.
investment_thesis:
The screen’s five-family pass describes a mid-teens earnings multiple and a 4.6% trailing yield on a diversified miner, not a confirmed through-cycle cash compounder. Passed models are Graham Enterprising, Neff PEGY, Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Economic Moat, High Dividend Yield, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Acquirer’s Multiple, Composite Value and Financial Health. Conflict check versus `screen_run_manifest.json` (not visible to the screen worker): the eleven non-passes are Graham Defensive, Graham Net-Net, Schloss, Deep Value, Earnings Yield (0.61), FCF Yield (0.30), Low P/E + High Yield, Lynch PEG, Dreman Contrarian, Piotroski and Earnings Quality. Snapshot failed_models remains []. P/E 13.7, P/B 2.5, yield 4.6%, ROE 19.3% and D/E 32% are screen prints; they have not been replaced by a statutory FY2025 note. Data quality 20/20 does not repair an empty failed-model list, a suppressed TTM cash-flow field, or cyclical flags that never fired.

For a value investor the hook is still cash and the ordinary dividend — if, and only if, company-definition USD free cash flow covers a 50% underlying-earnings payout after development capex, Simandou, Rincon and residual acquisition cash, and if the copper/aluminium price step-up in H1 is not the entire quality/moat/ROE stack. H1 2026 is the first assigned body that shows the mix: Iron Ore still the largest segment at $6.8 billion underlying EBITDA (−1%), Copper $5.7 billion (+84%), Aluminium & Lithium $3.3 billion (+38%). That is a copper-and-price residual as much as an iron-ore volume story. Pilbara realisations were only +2% ($92.6/dmt); copper +35% and aluminium +39% did the work.

It is not a strong buy on this pack. The 2 September overlay already tried to downgrade to Buy on FCF-yield and earnings-quality fails; the snapshot then undid that brake. One-year total shareholder return of 72% and a Morgan Stanley ADR Underweight at $90 (news-only, more than 14% implied downside, not a research target) sit next to a one-week new print. Size any book as accumulate, in USD filing terms, and do not use the £7,153.82-class limits until they are restated as pence or as pounds.
financial_review:
Reporting currency on the H1 body and on the Yahoo annual block is US dollars. Prefer the H1 filing over Yahoo except where workers flagged the statutory FY pack as absent — which they did. PRIMARY-FILING GAP: the assigned annual slot is a publication notice, not the 19 February 2026 Annual Report or the 20-F. filings_index.json body_path values point at docs/data/research/RIO.L and output/research/RIO.L, outside this trial tree. Period coverage annual=20 / interim=47 / trading_update=0 counts AGM notices, Companies House accounts, SVM collab items and the Tomago RNS as annual, and dumps SEC 6-Ks plus IR-allowlist 20-F copies into interim.

Assigned “annual” — not results. 2025 Annual Report notice to ASX/LSE (`/workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/RIO.L/20260904T183631Z/sources/filings/bodies/a395d7da4dca5b2b.txt`; Investegate, published 2026-02-19, catalog period=annual, priority 120). Annual-worker status partial: this is an RNS that the report was released on riotinto.com/reports, that a Form 20-F was expected on or around the same day, and that companion sustainability documents exist. Authorised by Group Company Secretary Andy Hodges. No reporting currency, statutory versus underlying EBITDA/earnings/EPS, segment split, Pilbara shipments, OCF, capex, company FCF, cash versus restricted cash versus net debt, leases, dividend declared versus paid, buybacks, Arcadium/M&A cash, impairments, pensions, or jurisdictional risk language appear on the page.

Assigned “interim” — H1 2026 results. Rio Tinto 2026 half year results (`/workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/RIO.L/20260904T183631Z/sources/filings/bodies/e36747cb4ebb850b.txt`; Investegate, published 2026-07-29, catalog period=interim). Interim-worker status partial: narrative and tables are present; the extract is truncated mid-Directors’ Report, so APM reconciliations, the full balance sheet and the statutory income statement after that cut are not in this body. H1 2025 comparatives are restated for the 27 August 2025 organisational restructure; Rio Tinto share of capital investment comparatives are also restated after an H2 2025 methodology change to include asset sales. Free cash flow is refined from H1 2026 to include Rio Tinto share of capital investment. No full FY2025 P&L restatement is in this extract.

Group H1 2026 versus H1 2025, same body. Underlying EBITDA $14.8 billion (+28% versus $11.5 billion); underlying earnings $6.9 billion (+43% versus $4.8 billion); net earnings (PAT attributable) $6.7 billion (+47% versus $4.5 billion); underlying EPS 421.4 US cents (+42% versus 296.0); consolidated sales revenue $31.0 billion (+15% versus $26.9 billion). Segment underlying EBITDA: Copper $5.7 billion (+84% versus restated $3.1 billion); Iron Ore $6.8 billion (−1% versus restated $6.9 billion); Aluminium & Lithium $3.3 billion (+38% versus restated $2.4 billion); reportable segments total $15.8 billion (+28%). Copper, aluminium and lithium together were more than 50% of group underlying EBITDA.

Cash and capital, same H1 body. Net cash from operating activities $9.2 billion (+32% versus $6.9 billion). Rio Tinto share of capital investment $5.0 billion (+12% versus restated $4.5 billion): growth $1.3 billion, sustaining $1.8 billion, replacement $1.9 billion, decarbonisation $0.04 billion. Free cash flow $3.8 billion (+75% versus $2.2 billion). Underlying EBITDA cash conversion 62% (+2pp). Working-capital outflow $1.6 billion; $443 million Oyu Tolgoi tax payment. Net debt $14.1 billion at 30 June 2026 versus $14.4 billion at 31 December 2025 (−$0.3 billion in H1). Cash and equivalents plus short-term liquid investments $9.1 billion (versus $9.2 billion). Net gearing 16% (versus 18%). Interim ordinary dividend declared $3.4 billion, 211 US cents per share (+43% versus 148 US cents), 50% payout ratio; payment date 24 September 2026. Dividends paid to equity shareholders in H1 $4.2 billion (2025 final ordinary). Taxes and government royalties $5.6 billion (versus $4.8 billion). Effective tax rate on underlying earnings 25.2%; FY2026 guide lowered to about 25% (was about 30%), expected about 30% from 2027.

Shipments, realisations and costs, same H1 body. Pilbara production 162.3 Mt (+6%) and shipments 157.7 Mt (+5%); highest H1 production since 2018. Total iron ore sales 164.5 Mt (includes Pilbara, IOC 6.5 Mt (−19%), Simandou 0.4 Mt). Copper production 442 kt (+1%). LCE production 27.3 kt (+53% versus the post-Arcadium H1 2025 comparative). Pilbara realised FOB $92.6/dmt (versus $90.5); copper 591 US c/lb (versus 436); aluminium $4,343/t (versus $3,125); LCE $18,960/t (versus $15,580). Pilbara unit cash costs $25.0/wmt FOB, at the top of the maintained $23.5–25.0 guide. Copper C1 net unit costs −24.7 US c/lb on gold by-product and productivity; 2026 C1 guide cut on 15 July to 30–50 c/lb from 65–75. Copper: Oyu Tolgoi ramp-up; Kennecott/Escondida lower; Kennecott flash-furnace breach late June — refined copper/gold lower in H2 but full-year copper including matte unchanged. Simandou: first sales April; H1 sales 0.4 Mt at 65.8% Fe; 2.2 Mt shipped to China; SimFer mine about 77% and port about 85% complete; 2026 sales guide 5–10 Mt maintained. Lithium: first production at Fénix 1B and Sal de Vida ahead of plan in Q2; Rincon full-scale plant toward about 200 ktpa LCE by 2028; starter-plant ramp focused on reactor stability. Aluminium: AP60 first hot metal March 2026; Boyne smelter secured an A$2 billion Queensland/Commonwealth package (March); Yarwun to cut alumina output 40% from October 2026. No Tomago reference in this body. Glencore: preliminary combination discussions announced 9 January 2026; Rio Tinto ceased considering a merger/combination on 5 February 2026.

Guidance path (FY February → cyclone March → Q2/H1 July → missing Q3). H1 states 2026 production and sales guidance maintained, subject to weather impacts; Pilbara also subject to mining-area approvals and heritage clearances. Unit-cost and share-of-capital-investment guidance maintained. Live ranges in this body: Pilbara shipments 323–338 Mt; total iron ore sales 343–366 Mt; Simandou 5–10 Mt; copper 800–870 kt; group share of capital investment up to $11.0 billion (H1 actual $5.0 billion). Pilbara Q1 cyclone about 8 Mt with about half expected recovered in 2026; productivity more than offset the cyclone in H1; H1 2026 cyclone EBITDA impact less than H1 2025; bauxite about 0.9 Mt Q1 weather impact with about half expected recovered. Guidance is held/maintained in this release, not narrowed or cut; the live changes are the tax rate and the copper C1 range. Q2-only tonnes were not extracted (separate 15 July RNS unread). Q3 2026 production is not in the corpus.

risks_and_flags:
Screen and overlay disagreement. Snapshot strong_buy / conviction 0.689 / failed_models=[] contradicts the same-run manifest adjusted_signal=buy / conviction 0.439 / FCF Yield and Earnings Quality fails. Summary text still says “Conviction 44%” and “overlay adjusted to Buy” while overlay booleans are all false. Composite 0.679 sits below the sector composite 0.725; the summary’s “sector-relative 72%” is the sector benchmark, not Rio outperforming the sector. Do not treat 11/22 and five families as a clean strong_buy. This trial does not recycle the snapshot’s pre-seeded accumulate boilerplate as if it were an independent confirmation.

Cyclical commodity and China concentration. cyclical_exposure_detected and cyclical_exposure_overlay are false. H1 realisations show why that is the wrong prior: copper +35%, aluminium +39%, lithium +22%, Pilbara iron ore only +2%. Iron ore remains the largest EBITDA line. China steel, copper TC/RC and lithium prices are the earnings engine. A mean-reversion in copper or aluminium would take the quality/GARP/ROE stack with it. Customer concentration on seaborne iron ore into China is not quantified in assigned bodies and is not thereby absent.

FCF versus the 4.6% yield. Yahoo FY2025 FCF 4,497 million versus dividends paid 6,145 million, screen FCF 3,596 million, and H1 company FCF $3.8 billion versus $4.2 billion cash paid, are enough to break High Dividend Yield and Dividend Growth if H2 cash or the unread company FY FCF disappoints. The H1 50% payout on underlying earnings is the live policy print. Trailing yield can be an artefact of 2025’s “top-end” cash payout (news titles only) after FCF had already fallen from Yahoo 5,978 million.

Leverage, M&A and project cash calls. Yahoo net debt 5.6 billion to 15.0 billion and company net debt still $14.1 billion after a $0.3 billion H1 reduction. Financial Health passed on screen D/E 32% and is only partly validated by H1 gearing 16%. Restricted cash 1,968 million, leases 1,586 million, Simandou completion, Rincon full-scale, residual 6,022 million purchase-of-business cash and unread Tomago/Boyne power spend are not in the screen’s risk family. JV recourse is not in assigned bodies.

Jurisdiction, heritage and climate. The FY notice only points at separate sustainability documents. 20-F risk factors, Simandou/Oyu Tolgoi/Australia heritage language and closure-provision notes were not assigned. H1’s $443 million Oyu Tolgoi tax payment and “subject to weather / heritage clearances” line are not a substitute for unread 20-F risk factors.

Glencore optionality. January–February 2026 talks ended over price (H1 body: discussions announced 9 January, ceased 5 February). 4 August news says Rio will not rush to revive the deal as the standstill ended. Treat it as parked headline optionality and a capital-allocation risk the risk family cannot see — not as a live bid, and not as dead by filing.

Aluminium power and competing capex. Tomago long-term power to 2038 and a news-cited A$1.1 billion commitment (13 August) are not in the H1 body; the Tomago RNS was not assigned. Boyne A$2 billion Queensland funding is an H1 mention without a contracted power price. Rio’s share, PPA price and aluminium-margin impact are unknown. That spend competes with Simandou, Rincon and the FY2025 acquisition cash. Yarwun’s 40% alumina cut from October 2026 is an operating residual already on the page.

Governance and execution. CEO succession (May 2025 RNS), August 2025 operating-model reset, 2026 AGM results, May 2026 Chief Legal Officer / Group Company Secretary appointments and July–September PDMR/employee-share issuance sit next to dual-listed PLC/Ltd voting. None of that is in the assigned annual notice or the truncated H1 directors’ table. Conviction 0.69 on a one-week snapshot is not a governance read. Kennecott’s late-June furnace breach is an H2 execution watch, not a full-year copper-guide cut.

Unit hygiene and dual-list. Summary limits of £7,153.82 / £6,905.37 with ATR 198.6 are pence mislabelled as pounds against a news LSE print of about £75.77. trade_plan is null. If those strings are pence, the live print is already through the core limit. Do not size sterling risk on those strings. ADR versus LSE versus ASX divergence is untested here (macro GBP/USD 1.3543 on 4 September is unused by the ladder).

It is not adequate in practice: period_coverage annual=20 / interim=47 / trading_update=0 counts AGM notices/results, Payments to Governments, a Supplementary Prospectus, SVM “Rio collab concludes”, and the Tomago power RNS as annual, and dumps ~40 SEC 6-Ks plus three IR-allowlist year-end HTMs (rio-2023/24/25, null published_at) into interim. Production reports that should be trading_update sit as interim. yahoo_quarterly_cashflow sits on the ladder but is empty (expected for a USD half-year reporter) while alternate_news is absent. filings_index.body_path values point at docs/data/research/RIO.L or output/research/RIO.L rather than this trial tree, and source_inventory counts 113 body files vs 118 indexed bodies even though every indexed basename is present.

Mandatory annual+interim summarize_filing_body plus news+screen+gap consumes the five-task cap even when the right FY and H1 bodies are chosen. There is no type or period flag for trading_update (Q1/Q2 production), 20-F, rns_cluster (PDMR/TVR/employee shares), mineral-resources, power_contract (Tomago/Boyne), or catalog_period_mismatch (Tomago/SVM/AGM tagged annual; IR 20-F HTMs tagged interim). gap_inventory can only list that the 20-F, H1 presentation, Q2 production, mineral-resources update, and Tomago/Boyne RNSs were dropped — it cannot assign them.

weeks_at_signal=1 / stability=new / improving already marks a fresh print, but there is no watch schema for: mid-October Q3 production (absent from a 4 Sep 17:26Z fetch), 2026 guidance vs cyclone-held levels, FCF vs the 4.6% dividend after H1, net-debt path after 15bn Yahoo net debt, Glencore standstill follow-up, Tomago/Boyne cash calls, Morgan Stanley ADR PT vs LSE pence limits, dual-list (RIO.L / RIO.AX / NYSE:RIO) price divergence, or snapshot adjusted_signal disagreeing with the overlay text in the same object. RSI 53 + price>50>200 timing=neutral is not a substitute. News freshness stops at 2 Sep; filings_index fetched 17:26Z on 4 Sep — a two-day news stall, not a filings stall. This trial re-asks the same 17:26Z catalog without new evidence.
